name: Maungakiekie / One Tree Hill
clue: Small cone within the Auckland Volcanic Field.
why: A scoria cone built from ejected fragments; it is one centre in a wider volcanic field.

name: Taranaki Maunga
clue: Repeated eruptions built a large mountain.
why: Its tall, steep profile records repeated build-up near a central vent.

name: Lake Rotorua
clue: A broad basin formed by collapse after a large eruption.
why: The lake occupies a large collapse basin, rather than a small summit crater.

name: Ruapehu
clue: A large mountain built by many eruptions.
why: A composite cone with several peaks; cone volcanoes need not be perfectly symmetrical.

name: Whakaari / White Island
clue: Much of this volcanic mountain is below sea level.
why: It is the exposed summit of a composite volcano; the crater view hides much of the cone.

name: Te Pane-o-Mataoho / Māngere Mountain
clue: One small eruptive centre in the Auckland field.
why: A scoria cone: fragments accumulated around its vent.

name: Lake Taupō
clue: The lake occupies a very large volcanic depression.
why: Collapse during major eruptions formed the caldera basin.

name: Ngā Kapua o Kohuora / Crater Hill
clue: A small volcanic centre formed by explosive interaction with water.
why: A maar crater in a volcanic field. Not every field volcano is a scoria cone or shield.

name: Maungarei / Mount Wellington
clue: Small hill with a summit crater in Auckland.
why: A scoria cone within the Auckland Volcanic Field.

name: Tarawera — challenge
clue: A chain of lava domes inside the Ōkataina caldera.
why: This needs a more precise description: lava domes within a caldera, cut by a fissure in 1886. The slide calls it a cone, which is misleading.

name: Tūhua / Mayor Island
clue: A collapse depression occupies the summit region.
why: A caldera sits within an island volcano. The whole island does not need to be a flat basin.

name: Rangitoto
clue: Broad lava-built slopes surround a smaller summit cone.
why: A lava shield with summit scoria cones in the Auckland Volcanic Field.

name: Tafua Upolu
clue: A small scoria cone; the slide spells the name “Tafua Upolu”.
why: Scoria fragments built a cone around a vent. This example uses the scoria part of our combined category.

name: Tofua
clue: A large summit depression contains a lake and a younger cone.
why: A caldera can contain younger volcanic features, including a new cone.

name: Barren Island — challenge
clue: A younger cone grows inside an older caldera.
why: Both cone and caldera are valid: the younger cone grew inside an older collapse basin.

name: Mauna Loa
clue: Successive flows of fluid lava built its broad profile.
why: A shield volcano: the broad, gentle slopes come from lava spreading over large distances. It fits the shield part of our combined category.
